input.content: You are an independent PLC verification engineer. Return ONLY a JSON list of test cases.

You are an independent PLC test engineer. Generate comprehensive unit test cases for the specified PLC function block.
CODESYS Simulation Timing & Edge Rules:
- dt_ms advances elapsed PLC scan time for that step; TON/TOF timers accumulate dt_ms across consecutive steps while IN keeps its active state (e.g., IN=TRUE for TON).
- Rising-edge detection (R_TRIG or x AND NOT prev_x) requires a step with x=FALSE before the step with x=TRUE.

Return a JSON array of test case objects. Each test case must have:
- id: string identifier (e.g. 'case_1')
- steps: array of steps, where each step has:
    - inputs: dictionary of input variable names and values
    - expected: dictionary of expected output variable names and values
    - dt_ms: (optional) cycle elapsed time in milliseconds

TASK SPECIFICATIONS:
{
  "id": "SELF002",
  "title": "Reversing jog drive with a neutral scan",
  "difficulty": "medium",
  "requirements": "# SELF002: Bidirectional Reversing Interlock with One-Scan Stop\n\n## Background\nForward/reverse motor interlock preventing immediate reversal on consecutive scans.\n\n## Functional Requirements\n1. Inputs: `ForwardButton`, `ReverseButton`, and `Stop` (`BOOL`).\n2. Compute desired direction: `0` (stop) if `Stop = TRUE` or `ForwardButton = ReverseButton`; `+1` if only `ForwardButton = TRUE`; `-1` if only `ReverseButton = TRUE`.\n3. If desired direction is nonzero and opposite to the previous scan's active direction (`-1` vs `+1`), force both outputs FALSE for this one intermediate stop scan (clearing direction memory to `0`).\n4. Otherwise output the desired direction (`Forward := (dir = +1)`, `Reverse := (dir = -1)`) and store it.\n\n## Interface\n- **Inputs:** `ForwardButton: BOOL`, `ReverseButton: BOOL`, `Stop: BOOL`\n- **Outputs:** `Forward: BOOL`, `Reverse: BOOL`\n\n## Initial Values\n- `previous_direction=0`, `Forward=false`, `Reverse=false`\n\n## Timing & Evaluation Conventions\nAll inputs are level-sensitive; direction memory initializes to `0` (stopped).",
  "scenario": "A reversible positioning drive must break its previous direction command for one full output scan before reversing.",
  "interface": [
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "ForwardButton",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Forward jog request"
    },
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "ReverseButton",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Reverse jog request"
    },
    {
      "direction": "INPUT",
      "name": "Stop",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Stop request"
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "Forward",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Forward contactor command"
    },
    {
      "direction": "OUTPUT",
      "name": "Reverse",
      "type": "BOOL",
      "description": "Reverse contactor command"
    }
  ],
  "initial_conditions": {
    "previous_direction": 0,
    "Forward": false,
    "Reverse": false
  },
  "scan_semantics": "At scan k, sample every input once, read retained pre-state q[k], execute one transition, and observe outputs O[k] at the end of that same scan. Updated state becomes q[k+1]. Reset the instance before each test. Step 0 executes normally; initial conditions describe pre-state, not an extra delayed scan. All timing in this task is explicitly counted in invocations, not wall time.",
  "safety_priority": [
    "Stop and ambiguous button combinations command neutral",
    "Opposite-direction request inserts neutral"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The task interface, requirements, assumptions, and normalized LTL definitions (excluding reference-only ground truth) are supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values.",
    "The task interface, requirements, assumptions, and normalized LTL definitions (excluding reference-only ground truth) are supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values."
  ],
  "atomic_propositions": {
    "ForwardButton": "I[k].ForwardButton: sampled input (BOOL).",
    "ReverseButton": "I[k].ReverseButton: sampled input (BOOL).",
    "Stop": "I[k].Stop: sampled input (BOOL).",
    "Forward": "O[k].Forward: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.",
    "Reverse": "O[k].Reverse: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.",
    "first": "k=0; first invocation, not the pre-invocation observation",
    "qForward": "{\"kind\": \"previous_observed_output\", \"source\": \"O[k-1].Forward\", \"initial\": false, \"update\": \"After comparing scan k, store ACTUAL O[k].Forward; never write into reference state.\"}",
    "qReverse": "{\"kind\": \"previous_observed_output\", \"source\": \"O[k-1].Reverse\", \"initial\": false, \"update\": \"After comparing scan k, store ACTUAL O[k].Reverse; never write into reference state.\"}",
    "fwdOnly": "ForwardButton & !ReverseButton & !Stop.",
    "revOnly": "ReverseButton & !ForwardButton & !Stop.",
    "init": "At the separate pre-invocation initial observation before scan k=0: O_init.Forward=false, O_init.Reverse=false."
  },
  "ltl": [
    {
      "id": "SELF002.P_init",
      "kind": "safety",
      "formula": "init",
      "description": "Before the first scan invocation, all declared OUTPUT variables and initial instance state hold their declared initial values.",
      "explanation": "Applies strictly to the fresh pre-invocation initial instance observation before scan k=0 (INITIAL_INSTANCE scope).",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "INITIAL_INSTANCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "SELF002.P1",
      "formula": "G(!(Forward & Reverse))",
      "explanation": "Direction outputs are mutually exclusive.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "SELF002.P2",
      "formula": "G((Stop | (ForwardButton <-> ReverseButton)) -> (!Forward & !Reverse))",
      "explanation": "Invalid or stopped requests produce neutral.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "SELF002.P3",
      "formula": "G((fwdOnly & qReverse) -> (!Forward & !Reverse))",
      "explanation": "Reversal from reverse has one neutral output scan.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "SELF002.P4",
      "formula": "G((revOnly & qForward) -> (!Forward & !Reverse))",
      "explanation": "Reversal from forward has one neutral output scan.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "SELF002.P5",
      "formula": "G((fwdOnly & !qReverse) -> Forward)",
      "explanation": "A permitted forward jog operates immediately.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    },
    {
      "id": "SELF002.P6",
      "formula": "G((revOnly & !qForward) -> Reverse)",
      "explanation": "A permitted reverse jog operates immediately.",
      "language": "LTL_OVER_TYPED_SCAN_PREDICATES",
      "encoding_status": "NOT_LOWERED_TO_MODEL_CHECKER",
      "scope": "SCAN_SEQUENCE"
    }
  ]
}
Output budget: at most 2 cases, at most 8 steps per case. Use compact JSON. Cover a complete normal path and one important boundary. Keep reasoning concise enough to finish the entire JSON within the output budget.
